title: A Dual Ensemble Kalman Filter Approach to Robust Control of Nonlinear Systems: the robust-control proposition for the nonlinear model
author: Anant A. Joshi, Saviz Mowlavi, Mouhacine Benosman
work: A Dual Ensemble Kalman Filter Approach to Robust Control of Nonlinear Systems: An Application to Partial Differential Equations
difficulty_reason:
Counted unit: the paper's robust-control proposition for the nonlinear affine-in-control system, printed as the second of the paper's two Propositions (source0.tex lines 440--443), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 444--457. The statement is that using the control u = u-bar + u_d renders the system x-dot = a(x) + b(x)u + d(t,x) asymptotically stable, where u-bar is a control law assumed to stabilize the undisturbed system with a strictly positive definite Lyapunov function V whose derivative is negative along the undisturbed controlled trajectories, where b(x) has rank n for all x, and where the disturbance is bounded in norm by a known function lambda with |d| strictly below lambda; the robustifying term is u_d = -(lambda/|grad V|) b-dagger grad V with b-dagger the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.

The author's proof is complete and short: it follows the Lyapunov redesign method of Khalil Chapter 14.2, differentiates V along the trajectories of the disturbed closed loop, splits the derivative into the undisturbed part (which is negative by hypothesis) plus the terms produced by the robustifying control and by the disturbance, bounds the two new terms by |d| times |grad V| and by -lambda times |grad V| using Cauchy-Schwarz, and concludes that the derivative is bounded above by (|d| - lambda) times |grad V|, which is strictly negative because |d| is strictly below lambda. The proof then closes by recording, from the rank hypothesis on b(x) and the properties of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, that b b-dagger grad V equals grad V, so that the robustifying term indeed contributes the exact negative multiple of |grad V| that the estimate uses.

This is the paper's main theoretical claim for the nonlinear model, and it is the result the paper's title and abstract advertise for nonlinear systems: the whole design recipe, including the assumption set on b and on the disturbance bound and the use of the pseudoinverse so that no explicit model of the disturbance channel is needed, is organized around it, and it is the more general of the paper's two propositions (the first one is its linear special case, in which the same argument is carried out with the quadratic Lyapunov function of the algebraic Riccati equation). The individual ingredients are standard in a graduate nonlinear-control course, so the unit is not a research-level novelty in its technique, but the complete assembled claim for the general nonlinear affine-in-control class, with the rank condition and the pseudoinverse projection making the disturbance-cancelling term exact, is above the level of an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, where at most the linear special case with a matching disturbance channel would be posed. That places the unit in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
